label: Gerizim · precinct & mansion
source: Magen 2008, NEAEHL 5 p. 1743 site plan; pp. 1745–1747
credit: Original project diagram of selected published structural relations. Simplified outlines; omitted walls are not absent remains.
limit: Placed by imagery: Magen's site plan (p. 1743) and precinct plan (p. 1746) were registered to 2023 satellite imagery (stated accuracy 5 m; the plans agree within 1–2 m), and the model's parts stand at their drawn places. The precinct core follows the precinct plan's walls; the other parts are reported envelopes. Selected Hellenistic precinct and Area P envelopes only; the source also includes Persian, Byzantine and later remains. Staircases elsewhere and the courtyard cistern are described separately. The cistern and P5178 are not located by this overview. The Persian view follows the description in Magen et al. 2004 p. 3*.

features.label: Eastern monumental staircase · source no. 4
features.description: A staircase up to 23 m wide and 34 m long rises 15.5 m by about 57 steps to the upper gate. The eastern approach belongs to the Hellenistic precinct.
features.limit: The staircase is distinct from the southern seven-step flight and the 15-step flight at E1. No particular step is identified with entry 57, and its use in the scroll’s period is unresolved.

features.label: Mansion · Area P, source no. 15
features.description: The approximately 40 × 40 m mansion lies west of the sacred precinct. Its building IV is approximately 20 × 14 m and contains a stone-paved courtyard with a cistern.
features.limit: The overview locates the mansion envelope, not the cistern mouth. Festus specimen K35264 is catalogued at P5178; the exact installation and deposition context remain unknown.

features.label: Western entrance · source no. 10
features.description: The overall site plan distinguishes a western entrance from the eastern monumental staircase. The southern wing’s separate 9 m wide staircase retains seven steps.
features.limit: This selection locates source no. 10 only. The overall plan does not equate every entrance with the southern seven-step flight or locate the scroll’s upper pit.

features.label: Southeastern citadel · source no. 7
features.description: The Hellenistic precinct includes a southeastern citadel reported as 25 × 24 m, built around a central courtyard.
features.limit: A citadel courtyard supplies no independent identification or date for entry 57’s step and upper pit.

features.label: Persian-period precinct and gates
features.description: Magen, Misgav & Tsfania 2004: the temple was built in the 5th century BCE; the Persian precinct measured 96 × 98 m including its gates (about 200 × 200 cubits), with gates on the north (six-chambered, fully exposed), south and east and none on the west, because of its nearness to the back of the temple. Remains of a stair to the east gate lie under the second-phase stair. In the Hellenistic phase the south side was doubled and a fortress added in the south-east corner.
features.limit: The precinct is drawn on the core walls of Magen's precinct plan, registered to imagery. The pages read give no plan scale for the gates; their sizes in the model are illustrative.
sources: Magen, Misgav & Tsfania 2004 pp. 1, 3*, 8, 12–14; Fig. 5 key

features.limit: The figure establishes water-storage context. Cistern positions and fortress chronology cannot date or identify a separate drying installation or guard-post corner.

label: Hyrcania · pools, bridge & cisterns
source: Patrich 1989 Fig. 22, p. 256; double-pool description p. 255; Patrich 2002 pp. 336–352; Feldman (Ilan ed.) pp. 326–335
credit: Original project diagram of selected published structural relations. Simplified outlines; omitted walls are not absent remains.
limit: Placed by imagery: Patrich 1989 Fig. 22 was registered to 2023 satellite imagery (stated accuracy 5 m; the figure's page-up lies about 4.75° west of north), and the installations stand where the figure draws them, each on the modern terrain at its own place. Selected water installations only. The basin-centre and rim distance origins remain separate, unresolved hypotheses. The east bridge, pit and point 49 tunnel follow Patrich 2002's dimensions; the Herodian view is a reconstruction of the bridge to its 12.5 m channel. The placement is for display and tests nothing.

annotations.text: Source orientation · page-up ≈ 4.75° west of north

features.label: Northern member of the double pool
features.description: Patrich reports unequal sides of 19, 15, 18.2 and 16 m and a depth reaching about 5 m for the northern pool.
features.limit: The report’s plaster typology is not a sealed construction date. Entry 29’s reading, compass direction and distance origin must be selected independently.

features.label: Southern member of the double pool
features.description: The adjacent southern member is shallower, reaching about 2.6 m. Approximately 4.8–5.4 m of quarried rock separates the two members.
features.limit: A general 5 m pool depth cannot be assigned to this shallower basin. The pair’s survival does not identify a scroll reservoir.

features.label: East aqueduct bridge · source no. 48
features.description: The east bridge crosses the saddle between the double pool (north) and the southern pool. Patrich 2002: 112 m long; preserved up to about 6 m high, 2.5 m wide at the base and 1.45 m at the top; a few lower courses Hasmonean, the rest Herodian; the Herodian channel ran about 12.5 m above the base and is not preserved. Feldman gives the eastern saddle wall as 170 m long and 16.78 m high.
features.limit: The bridge is drawn straight along the line Fig. 22 draws, its foot on today's terrain and its top level, 6 m above the saddle's lowest point; its preserved height varies. The Herodian view's upper wall and channel are a reconstruction; Patrich also offers upper arches or a siphon. Neither phase dates a pool edge or selects an entry-29 datum.

features.label: Separate filled southern pool
features.description: A distinct quarried pool south of the bridge: a depression with a vertical rock-cut west side and no visible plaster (Patrich 2002). Patrich takes the area with the north pools as a kind of moat cutting the fortress off from the western ridge.
features.limit: Keep it separate from the double pool. Its function and phase remain uncertain.

features.label: Southern cisterns · D and F
features.description: The fort’s southern slope contains cisterns labelled separately in Fig. 22. Cisterns S and F receive their own detail figures on p. 258.
features.limit: These are other installations, rather than sections through the double pool. Their steps cannot substitute for a pool rim or contemporaneous conduit junction.

features.label: Round pit north-east of the north pool
features.description: A round pit 3.05 m in diameter and 4.3 m deep north-east of the north pool; its purpose is unknown (Patrich 2002 p. 348, Fig. 23).
features.limit: It is set at the round cistern that Fig. 22 draws north-east of the double pool; that this is Patrich 2002's pit is the project's inference. It is not a pool rim or conduit junction.

features.label: Built tunnel · point 49
features.description: Between cisterns A and N the aqueduct passes through a built, barrel-vaulted tunnel: free part about 11.5 m long, 1.25 m high and 0.75 m wide, with a square opening at the north end; the south end is blocked by débris (Patrich 2002 p. 351, Figs. 25a–b; the 1989 dimensions repeated).
features.limit: It is set at Fig. 22's (49); its exact course is not drawn there. The free length is what can be entered today; the tunnel's full length under the débris is not known. The 14/40/41-cubit test is unchanged by this record.

label: Abu Saraj · IV/17 cave
credit: Ofer Sion / Israel Antiquities Authority · CC BY-NC 4.0. Complete Plan 5 figure crop; source caption, scale and north arrow retained.
limit: No geographic registration. Complete published Plan 5 figure cropped from p. 63; no rotation or annotation baked into the image. Numbered selection markers are separate. The north arrow defines the right opening as northern. Present gaps do not reconstruct ancient thresholds, wall phases or floor elevations.

features.label: Northern opening · right side of plan
features.description: The source describes a 0.8 m northern opening leading into a northern space approximately 2.2 × 4.5 m.
features.limit: The northern member is distinguished using the drawn north arrow. Its present-aperture chord supplies no ancient threshold elevation or digging origin.
sources: Sion 2002 pp. 62–63, Plan 5; IV/17 assessment, 2 October 2026

features.label: Rock-cut dividing pillar
features.description: A rock-cut pillar divides the northern and southern spaces. Plan 5 shows an interior route around the pillar’s inner end.
features.limit: Two-dimensional connectivity does not establish ancient passage clearance. A pillar resemblance is shared with comparison caves and supplies no unique identification.

features.label: Southern opening · partial masonry block
features.description: The southern mouth is partly blocked by a masonry wall, reported as 2.4 m long and 0.4 m thick. The southern space is approximately 2.15 × 4.20 m.
features.limit: Present gaps differ from the earlier full mouth. Wall foundation, threshold contacts and a sealed construction date require the L-656 field file.
sources: Sion 2002 p. 63, Plan 5; IV/17 phase audit

label: Historical survey · SWP Sheet XI
source: Conder & Kitchener, Map of Western Palestine (1880), Sheet XI; surveys 1872–1877
credit: Palestine Exploration Fund · 1:63,360 · public-domain cartography. Complete sheet, margins and source scale retained.
limit: Unregistered historical survey; no geographic registration is inferred from the source grid. The broad Shechem-sector selection is context, not an excavation footprint or individual Gerizim stair/cistern. Symbols do not establish ancient chronology.

features.label: Shechem-region survey context
features.description: Sheet XI places Shechem near its southeastern corner and depicts the surrounding terrain, routes and named sites as recorded by the nineteenth-century survey.
features.limit: The broad selection marks the regional context only. Use the separate Magen plan for precinct and mansion architecture; this sheet does not identify entry 57’s step, upper pit or P5178.
sources: SWP Sheet XI; PDF 11 in the supplied map set

label: Bethesda · pools & eastern complex
source: Duprez 1970 pp. 33–41 and Pl. II; Gibson 2005 pp. 286–287 and 2011 pp. 22–28; Pierre & Rousée 1981 pp. 23–25, Figs. 2–3
credit: Original project diagram of selected published dimensions and relations. Simplified outlines; omitted walls are not absent remains.
limit: Placed in its mapped setting: the dam is put on the centroid of OpenStreetMap's outline of the excavated pool area (82.6 × 51.6 m), unturned; uncertain by about 25 m. No geographic registration. The pools use published dimensions with an assumed angle; the eastern complex follows the relative arrangement of Duprez Pl. II, and its distance and bearing from the pools are schematic. Byzantine and Crusader structures are omitted. The royal-period view follows Pierre & Rousée 1981: the dam, the north pool and an open canal before the south basin.

features.label: Northern pool
features.description: Gibson gives the northern pool as about 53 × 40 m, a reservoir of about 21,200 m³. Pierre & Rousée (1981) take it as the earlier basin, created by the dam, with only its south-east corner assured.
features.limit: Its depth is not recorded in the sources read; the model's 10 m is that volume divided by its area, an inference. The 40 m side is drawn east–west because the dam that forms its south side is about 40 m long (inference).

features.label: Central dam and chimney
features.description: Duprez: the central dam is built above and rock below, 6.50 m wide at the top, with ashlar faces in courses of about 60 cm and a square chimney about 1 × 1 m and about 15 m deep behind its north face. Pierre & Rousée 1981: about 40 m long, 6 m wide at the top and more than 7 m at the base, at most 13 m high, on a rock base with 20 courses of about 50 cm; small openings every 2 m link the shaft to the north basin, and a slab-covered corridor about 2 m high left its foot.
features.limit: Von Wahlde gives the chimney as 12 m deep; the model uses Duprez's 15 m. Pierre & Rousée date the dam to the Judahite monarchy on building technique and textual association, without sealed finds.

features.label: Southern pool and its western steps
features.description: Duprez: sides of about 45 m (north), 50 m (east), 65 m (south) and 47 m (west), up to 14 m deep; its rock steps broke the current of incoming water. Gibson: hewn and built steps with landings along the whole western side (F306–309). Pierre & Rousée 1981 date it Hellenistic (Simon II, 220–195 BCE), later than and independent of the north basin.
features.limit: The four sides fix the outline only with an assumed angle: the north side is drawn east–west and the west side north–south. Step count, width and landings are illustrative. Duprez dates the pools to the 2nd century BCE; Gibson to Herod, 31–22 BCE.

features.label: Settling basin at the north-west corner
features.description: Duprez reports a settling basin at the southern pool's north-west corner, with an east wall 2.60 m high (Pl. VII, 1).
features.limit: Its size and exact position are not given; the 5 × 5 m box in the corner is illustrative, and the model starts the western steps south of it.

features.label: Cistern 1 (first installation)
features.description: A natural grotto about 8.50 m deep and 6 m across, roofed by rock, with three side openings that were blocked; the whole first installation is organised around it (Duprez). Coins of the complex run to 68 CE.
features.limit: The eastern complex's distance and bearing from the pools are schematic; Duprez's Pl. II gives relative positions only, and its scale is not recorded.

features.label: Threshold and jamb between grotto 6 and cistern 1
features.description: Duprez found a threshold and parts of a door jamb in place between grotto 6 and cistern 1 (Pl. IX, 1), of good work, in a building too destroyed to reconstruct.
features.limit: Duprez does not say that the doorway opened into cistern 1. The slab's size and orientation are illustrative.

features.label: Grotto 6 with its bath
features.description: A grotto reached by a stair from the north, with a small bath in its north-west corner at the back (Pl. XI).
features.limit: No dimensions are given; the size and depth are illustrative.

features.label: Grotto 5
features.description: 1.50 m wide, 2 m long and 1.50 m high, entered by four steps roughly cut in the rock (Pl. IX, 2); on Pl. II its steps are on its west side.
features.limit: The steps' side is read from the plan (inference). Its use is unknown.

features.label: Grottoes 2 and 3, basin 4 and bath 7
features.description: Grotto 2 lies north of cistern 1 with a small basin 2.50 m below its entrance; grotto 3 to the north-east with a rectangular basin; basin 4, about 30 cm deep, 3 m east of the cistern; bath 7 to the south.
features.limit: Sizes other than basin 4's depth and grotto 2's basin level are illustrative; positions follow Pl. II's arrangement only.

features.label: Rock-cut canal south of the dam
features.description: Pierre & Rousée 1981: from the foot of the dam's shaft the water ran south through a slab-covered corridor and dropped about 3 m into an open rock-cut canal at the valley bottom, about 1 m deep and 75 cm wide, straight and known for about 50 m. When the south basin was built the corridor was deepened about 2 m and the canal was vaulted under the basin.
features.limit: Only the royal-period view draws the canal, straight south from the corridor; its line under the south basin and its level against Duprez's 14 m basin depth cannot be placed from the reported figures. The authors' reading of the canal as feeding the Temple is an inference from its direction.

label: Golden Gate · Warren 1867–70
source: Warren 1884 Pl. VI (measured with its scale bar); SWP Jerusalem (Warren & Conder 1884) pp. 141–145, 221
credit: Original project diagram of measurements from a public-domain plate and its text. Simplified outlines; omitted structures are not absent remains.
limit: Placed in its mapped setting: the gatehouse centre is put on OpenStreetMap's Golden Gate building and the plate frame is turned 5.5° so the gatehouse runs along the building's long sides (84.5°); Warren's 24.8 × 17.3 m gatehouse matches the mapped 27 × 17 m building. No geographic registration; the frame is the plate's, rotated about 9° from north. Levels are from Warren's recorded feet; the ground between them is interpolated. The gallery is shown in a display cutaway.

features.label: Golden Gate building
features.description: Plate VI draws the Golden Gate as a dashed outline about 24.8 × 17.3 m (81 × 57 ft), its east side on the Haram wall line. SWP: probably a later reconstruction standing on the ancient foundations of a gateway; sill level 2,396 ft.
features.limit: The outline is the plate's, measured with its scale bar. The building's height, roof and twin passages are not drawn from a published source and are illustrative. The Herodian east gate may not lie exactly under it (record F12.4).

features.label: Haram east wall
features.description: Warren: at the Golden Gate the Sanctuary wall extends 30–40 ft below the present surface outside. From the gate south to the postern (51 ft) three courses of large stones with marginal drafts and rough projecting faces are visible.
features.limit: The model draws the wall straight along the gate outline's axis; the plate's line runs about 2.4° off it (up to 1.9 m at the model's ends). Thickness and height above the Haram surface are illustrative.

features.label: Cistern XV (Bir al-Tawba)
features.description: About 18 ft across and 35 ft deep, rock-cut with a rock roof (SWP p. 221); Gibson and Jacobson: one chamber about 5.5–5.8 m across, floor 10.7–11 m below the Haram, one square shaft entrance. Its centre is 30.0 m west of the gatehouse's west face on Plate VI. No recorded cistern lies within about 18 m of the gatehouse; entry 9's nineteen cubits is 8.5–10 m (record F12.4).
features.limit: The shaft entrance's size and position over the chamber are illustrative.

features.label: Massive wall in front of the gate
features.description: Met by Warren's gallery about 46 ft in front of the Golden Gate, running north and south and then turning west: large quarry-dressed blocks with rough drafts, courses 2 ft 6 in high and over 5 ft long, joints packed with small stones in a cement like that used for cisterns. A 5 ft 6 in hole did not reach its back. Large drafted stones lie on the same line at the surface.
features.limit: Plate VI draws its northern part; the model extends it 4.3 m south of the gallery, as the text reports, along the plate's line. Its base and thickness are unknown; the top is drawn at the present surface because SWP thinks it probably reaches it. It is not identified as a cistern.

features.label: Warren's 1869 shaft and gallery
features.description: A shaft sunk 55 ft 6 in below the ground outside the gate, 143 ft from it on the perpendicular from its south end, then 25 ft 6 in deeper; a gallery driven west, rising with the rock, through two rough masonry walls, to the massive wall at 97 ft. The square marked 2308 on Plate VI is, by inference, the shaft bottom.
features.limit: The gallery is drawn in a display cutaway trench, not an excavation. Its section, steps and the shaft's shape are illustrative; its rise follows the reported 8 ft at 37 ft and 25 ft 6 in at 85 ft. On the plate the massive wall lies about 54 ft from the Haram wall on this line; the text gives 46 ft. The model follows the plate.

features.label: Tank or rock-cut tomb
features.description: Crossed by the gallery 18 ft 6 in from the shaft, about 38 m east of the gate; 'the examination of this was reserved'.
features.limit: Its size and form are not recorded; only its position on the gallery line is shown.

features.label: Column shaft standing in the debris
features.description: At 68 ft from the shaft, part of a column shaft 3 ft in diameter stood erect in the debris about 3 ft above the rock, with what appear to be masons' marks on its base.
features.limit: Drawn beside the gallery so that it can be seen; its length is illustrative.

label: Bene Ḥezir & Zechariah · Avigad 1954
source: Avigad 1954, Ancient Monuments in the Kidron Valley, ch. 4 (pp. 37–73, 76–78), p. 79, Figs. 22–25, 42; English summary
credit: Original project diagram from Avigad's published measurements. Avigad's figures are not reproduced.
limit: Registered to the OpenStreetMap outlines of Bene Ḥezir, Zechariah and Absalom (a few metres): Avigad's frame is placed on the mapped porch and turned so that his 'west' is the mapped façade normal (about 245°; his 'south-west', p. 37). Ground pads, the valley floor level and the modern surroundings (OpenStreetMap, ODbL) are illustrative setting. Chambers are drawn as rectangles at mean dimensions; wall thicknesses, floor levels and the heights of Zechariah and Absalom are illustrative.

annotations.text: Registered to OpenStreetMap outlines · façade faces 245°

features.label: Bene Ḥezir façade and inscription
features.description: A Doric distylos in antis, 5.75 m long and 3.95 m high to the cornice, cut in a rock wall about 15 m high; its floor is about 8.50 m above the rock path. The façade faces south-west. The three-line architrave inscription names Eleazar, Ḥaniah, Yoʿezer, Judah, Simeon and Yoḥanan, sons of Joseph son of ʿObed, and Joseph and Eleazar sons of Ḥaniah, 'priests of the sons of Ḥezir' (Avigad's reading; ʿObed preferred to ʿOded).
features.limit: The façade's two parts meet at an obtuse angle; the model draws them in one plane and turns Avigad's 'west' to the mapped façade normal (about 245°). Avigad dates the façade to about the middle of the 2nd century BCE and the inscription to the first half of the 1st century BCE; nothing on these pages links the family or ʿObed with Jericho.

features.label: Porch, columns and north stair
features.description: Porch 5.55–5.83 × 3.04–3.23 m and 3.20–3.50 m high behind two baseless Doric columns (3.00 m, lower diameter 0.53–0.55 m). The present wide opening into the cave is not original: the first opening was about 80 cm wide, on the column axis. A stair 1.60 m wide comes down from the rock top through a breach in the north wall: 13 steps are visible, from 4.68 to 1.78 m above the floor, and its shaft breaks 0.80–1.20 m into the porch ceiling.
features.limit: Avigad explains the stair shaft as a surveying error by cutters working from above (pp. 48–49). Its upper part is under modern graves; the model continues it to the rock surface.

features.label: Chamber A and burial chambers B–E
features.description: A central chamber (A, 4.20–5.40 × 3.17–3.85 m, 2.20 m high) opens on three burial chambers: B (north, 3.35 × 3.50 m, two kokhim and a corner kokh), C (south, 4.00 × 3.60 m, four kokhim), D (east, 1.95 m high, a pit later deepened from 50 to 77 cm, two cells), and E beyond D (2.03 × 2.20 m, three arcosolia), the most carefully cut. In all nine kokhim, a tenth unfinished, and three arcosolia.
features.limit: Avigad gives no wall thicknesses or floor levels; the model draws 0.8 m walls and level floors. The north doorway of A and the porch doorway are lost in later breaches; the original-state view restores them.

features.label: South corridor to the Zechariah court
features.description: A corridor 8.30 m long and about 2.30 m wide continues the porch axis to the Zechariah court; six steps of 20–22 cm are visible and more lie under earth (Slouschz saw them). Its plain opening, 1.35 m wide, faces the north-west corner of Zechariah 3.08 m away.
features.limit: Avigad thinks the corridor is not contemporary with the tomb and defers the question to the Zechariah chapter, which was not photographed.

features.label: Added façade (the nefesh) and niche
features.description: North of the Doric façade a plain façade about 4 m high, divided into three strips, has a central recess 1.93 m wide with an opening 0.78 × 1.65 m into a niche 1.30 m deep. A hole in the niche floor leads to a small cell below. Avigad takes this façade, completed by a pyramid, as the inscription's 'nefesh' (Fig. 42, 1), not Zechariah.
features.limit: The pyramid is Avigad's reconstruction; he publishes no dimensions in the pages read and notes that the rock leaves no room for a square base without reaching over the stair behind (p. 76). Pp. 74–75 were not photographed.

features.label: Zechariah monument and court
features.description: A rock-cut monolith 5.50–5.60 m square, a cube with a pyramid, standing in a court of 11.20 × 11.45 m enclosed by rock walls on three sides (the north wall runs to 15.30 m); about 12 m south-east of the Bene Ḥezir façade. Avigad: apparently solid, a sepulchral monument rather than a tomb; its tombs may lie hidden in the rock to the east.
features.limit: Its base is buried and its height is not given in the pages read; the model's heights are illustrative. An unfinished tomb south of it (Fig. 25) is not drawn.

features.label: Absalom's monument
features.description: About 50 m from the Bene Ḥezir façade. Avigad's summary: 20 m high; a square rock-cut substructure with Ionic columns, a Doric frieze and an Egyptian cornice, a course of dressed stone, and a built round superstructure ending in a concave cone; a burial chamber with two arcosolia; the superstructure is the nefesh of the tomb beneath. Dated to the beginning of the 1st century CE.
features.limit: Only the height and the parts come from the pages read: the footprint, drum and cone in the model are illustrative massing. Its position and the turn of its sides are those of its OpenStreetMap outline. Chapter 6 (pp. 91–133) was not photographed.

label: The Great Sea (cistern VIII) · Warren Pl. VII
source: Warren 1884 Pl. VII (cistern VIII, 'The Great Sea'); Gibson & Jacobson 1996 pp. 33–39 (No. 3 = W8)
credit: C. Warren, Plans, Elevations, Sections, &c. (PEF 1884), Pl. VII, crop of the 600 ppi line art · public domain (BYU Library scan, Internet Archive).
limit: Registered through Warren's plate to the Haram's south corners as mapped by OpenStreetMap (about 1 m at the corners), so the cistern sits under the court north of al-Aqsa where the plate draws it. The modern surroundings (OpenStreetMap, ODbL) are setting, not evidence. The outline is the plate's hatching, traced at its scale bar and turned by its north arrow (±2 m). Piers, stair, two of the three mouths and the roof cutaway are illustrative or for display.

features.label: Cistern VIII, 'The Great Sea'
features.description: The largest cavity under the Ḥaram, south of the inner platform in front of the Aqṣā: rock-cut and plastered, about 40 × 30 m (Schick) or 44 × 45 m (Pierotti), 10–11.5 m high, its floor 13.3–14 m below the surface, with a rock roof about 2.5 m thick and a capacity of 9,100–12,000 m³. Warren's plate draws its hatched extent as about 37.7 × 48.4 m.
features.limit: Gibson & Jacobson give no date for its cutting in the pages read, and their 2nd-century BCE map marks other cisterns, not this one. A plastered cistern with one stair and several mouths does not by itself identify the scroll's 'great cistern'.

features.label: Shaft mouth drawn by Warren
features.description: Warren draws one small circle beside the label 'Cistern' inside VIII, read here as a mouth. Barclay counted 8 shafts with one open, Wilson 'a great many mouths, but only three are now in use', Schick four shafts 2.5 m deep.
features.limit: Reading the circle as a mouth is an inference. The other mouths are not placed by any source read; two in the model stand for Wilson's three in use.

features.label: Rock piers
features.description: Five free-standing rock piers (Schick); four piers and two rock partitions on Wilson's plan; 'a fine cavern with rocky piers' (W&C). The roof is partly rock and partly flat stones, with some vaulting.
features.limit: Warren's plate draws no piers. Their places and size in the model are illustrative.

features.label: Rock-cut stair from the south
features.description: A narrow rock-cut stair from the south or south-east: 44 steps (Barclay) or 50 (Schick), reached from 'a hole on the northern side of the workshops east of al-Aksa' (Wilson); Whitty saw a well-like mouth several feet deep with a ruined flight below. Barclay says the steps were partly re-cut 'only a few centuries ago'. Beyond one shaft a broad four-step stair, gone by 1887, 'may possibly have been a relic of the Herodian Temple complex' (Fig. 18 caption).
features.limit: The plate does not draw the stair; its line, width and top opening in the model are illustrative. No spiral stair is described on the Ḥaram in the pages read.
